body: To clarify, this uses an already existing mode in the rendering server that just isn't exposed on CanvasItem? If so it should probably reference this mode and how it relates to it

> this uses an already existing mode in the rendering server that just isn't exposed on CanvasItem?

Yes, similar to other ClipChildrenModes. Documenting the link between them and CanvasGroupModes makes sense. There is nothing about them [now](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_renderingserver.html#enum-renderingserver-canvasgroupmode). But I guess that would be a separate PR because it touches all ClipChildrenModes.

Just before too much time is put into this. I don't think this should be merged. It is super dangerous and may work currently for some use-cases, but is guaranteed to be totally broken for many types of nodes _and_ will be prone to breakage when seemingly unrelated areas of code are touched. 

CanvasGroup is designed as a special case of canvas item clipping. The CanvasGroup node is basically an empty shell with a few parameters that control how the texture is captured. All of the important logic happens inside the RenderingServer. **All of that logic assumes that the CanvasGroup is basically CanvasItem node with nothing else**. The logic:
1. Adds a rendering command (COMMAND_RECT)
2. Sizes and shapes the CanvasGroup to fit around its children
3. Affects the sorting of the CanvasGroup and its children

If any node can be a CanvasGroup, then all of that logic needs to change and we need to handle a bunch of cases we don't have now:
1. What happens when the node has CanvasItem commands that come _before_ the CanvasGroup command?
2. How does this interact with Control clipping? Control clipping works totally different from CanvasItem clipping
3. How do we handle resizing. The RenderingServer ignores sizing right now, but Control nodes actually care about their size and shape, so having the RenderingServer basically ignore that and do its own thing is an issue. 

In general I never support moving specialized functionality into a more general area. This PR, as-is, adds a lot of bloat to CanvasItem, which means it bloats pretty much every single 2D node for an extremely niche feature. 

Instead I would just add a new Control node that mirrors the functionality of CanvasGroup. It can be ultra small and avoid adding bloat. In fact, you can do that already in GDScript by using the RenderingServer API directly.

Thank you for the explanation! I see now it's more complicated than I thought. But I still think there's a feature disparity between Node2D and Control that should be addressed somehow. 

Given the concerns, I see three options:
1. Handle the edge cases in the current approach
2. Create a new Control-derived node
3. Document the GDScript workaround

As I've already started this, I'm ready to pursue any of the options. And in case we pick option 1 or 2, I've got a few things to clarify.

> control clipping

Haven't tested this before but I see the issues now. With `Control`, `clip_contents` overrides `clip_children` and the `ClipChildrenMode` from this PR does behave strange when `clip_contents` is `true` and the node is empty. If I understand it correctly, [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/295e465fe403954911ca75145cc5d21546274262/scene/gui/control.cpp#L3908) are the lines that need modification if we are to proceed with the "handle the edge cases" option. Is this correct? Or am I missing something?

> bloat

Could you clarify what do you mean by bloat? Extra code complexity/something memory-related/user confusion due to new features? Isn't `clip_children` functionality itself quite specialized but still in the base class? I ask to understand where's the threshold to what belongs in the base class vs a specialized node.

> how do we handle resizing?

Haven't encountered any bugs yet. Could you point to specific cases where they might arise?

> Could you clarify what do you mean by bloat? Extra code complexity/something memory-related/user confusion due to new features?

Both, in my opinion. To be clear, the problem is mainly the two additional properties, `fit_margin` and `use_mipmaps`, which this mode would heavily benefit on. Even if they're not used by most **CanvasItem** nodes, they'd still be stored, taking up a decent chunk of space (especially considering how common these nodes are), and risk making all nodes inheriting **CanvasItem** look more complicated than they are in practice.
